title: Microsoft Viva: identifiable export of Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The roadmap facts and most of the documented controls are supported. The mixed licensing classification is not established by the sources, and the briefing overstates what ordinary export delegation establishes about access to identifiable data. Both admin paths also stop before the access setting.

claims.quote: This enables users to export Identifiable row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis.

claims.claim: Delegation therefore extends who can see named data.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Dashboard" delegates "identifiable" access policy'. Read export-copilot-metrics, identification-copilot-analytics and delegate-access. Export inheritance is stated; inheritance of the separate identification permission is not.
claims.fix: Remove 'Delegation therefore extends who can see named data;' and retain the supported statement that delegates inherit data-export access unless the administrative policy disables it. The export page separately conditions identifiable fields on administrative enablement for the exporter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence specific to identifiable export is published beyond the existing prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard identifiable export license entitlement pricing prerequisites'. Read export-copilot-metrics, identification-copilot-analytics, copilot-dashboard and VFAM requirements; results name existing licences, not a separate identifiable-export licence.

claims.claim: Identifiable export has a mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard identifiable export license entitlement pricing prerequisites'. Read export-copilot-metrics, copilot-dashboard, feature-access-management and identification-copilot-analytics. No combination of distinct entitlement models is documented.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' under the standard's rule for an option inside an already licensed product. Retain the notes that export requires at least 50 assigned Copilot or Viva Insights licences and that no separate identifiable-export licence or price is published.

claims.claim: Creating VFAM policies requires a supported Microsoft 365 version or a Viva Suite licence.
claims.quote: Policy creation requires the following elements: A supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.

claims.claim: The documented VFAM access controls are unavailable in GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: Users with non-global access, such as managers with team-level views, cannot export.
claims.quote: Users with non-global access, such as managers with team-level views, can't access this feature to export data.

claims.claim: Processing can take up to seven days after licence assignment, except for day-level metrics.
claims.quote: Data processing in Copilot Analytics takes up to seven days following license assignment, unless you're exporting day-level metrics, which provides more recent data.

claims.claim: The export control documentation identifies Global Administrators as its administrators.
claims.quote: Copilot Metrics Export (Preview) | No | Global admin | Viva Insights

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell 3.2.0 or later is required for scripting VFAM policies.
claims.quote: Access to Exchange Online PowerShell Version 3.2.0 or later. If you need to use non-mail-enabled groups you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.5.1 or later.
claims.fix: Append 'Use version 3.5.1 or later for non-mail-enabled groups' to the scripting prerequisite, preserving the existing 3.2.0 minimum for other cases, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/manage-access-policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview contains VFAM policy creation, update and deletion history.
claims.quote: For a history of policy creation, updates, and deletions, see the Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) change logs for your organization in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy is the admin-centre route for an identification policy.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On'. The existing prefix is documented but stops in the policy-creation flow before selecting the feature and setting.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with VivaInsights, a discovered FeatureId, IsFeatureEnabled $true and Everyone enables identification tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Now that you have the featureID, use the Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy PowerShell cmdlet to create an access policy for the feature. ... by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.

claims.claim: Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy is the admin-centre route for controlling user-level exports.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. ... select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off' to match the row's disabling command. The existing prefix stops before the access setting.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with VivaInsights, a discovered FeatureId, IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone disables the export feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false -GroupIds ... -UserIds ... If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.

claims.claim: GroupIds or UserIds can replace Everyone to scope a policy to groups or individual users.
claims.quote: This example adds a policy for the Reflection feature in Viva Insights. The policy disables the feature for the specified users and group members. If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.
